overview: A rare anti-Sicilian that leads to a reversed English structure. White plays c4 and d3 or Nc3, Nf3 and often g3, aiming at a Maróczy-like bind. Black answers with ...Nc6 and ...g6, or ...e6 and ...d6, with an easy game. The play is slow and positional, without much theory.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nc3 and g3, with a bishop on g2 and d3 rather than d4
Control d5 and aim for a Maróczy-like bind if d4 is played

black_ideas.idea: ...Nc6, ...g6, ...Bg7 for a Dragon-like set-up and queenside play

typical_structures.structure: Reversed English; closed Sicilian pawn structure with c4 and e4

character.notes: Quiet and lightly forcing; no big attack for either side, equality is easy.

structure.notes: Sicilian-type asymmetric centre; I take flexible because both sides delay committing.

approach.notes: Standard but uncommon; a respectable anti-Sicilian.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...Nc6 3.Nc3 g6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. c4 Nc6 3. Nc3 g6
sublines_that_differ.how: Dragon-like set-up, Black fianchettoes and plays for ...d6 and ...Nf6.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor hard to break down; I am unsure of the main branch.

structure.reason: Sicilian pawn structure but the centre is undecided; Sicilians are usually semi-open.

approach.reason: A less common but respectable anti-Sicilian.

plans.reason: No clear characteristic plan from memory.
